Fit a BYM2 model with optional spatially varying coefficients

Source: R/models.R
svy_fit_bym2.Rd

Fits a unit-level (individual or cluster) model with a BYM2 area random effect using INLA. Covariates named in svc additionally get an area-specific slope, so their effect can vary across space.

Usage

svy_fit_bym2(
  data,
  formula,
  graph,
  area_col = "area_id",
  family = "binomial",
  Ntrials = NULL,
  E = NULL,
  svc = NULL,
  svc_model = c("besag", "bym2"),
  extra_terms = NULL,
  priors = svy_priors(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame (or sf object) with outcome, covariates and area identifiers, e.g. survey records joined to svy_extract() output.

formula

Fixed-effects formula, e.g. stunted ~ pm25 + urban.

graph

An svy_graph from svy_adjacency().

area_col

Area identifier column in data (and in graph$index).

family

INLA likelihood, e.g. "binomial", "poisson", "gaussian".

Ntrials

For binomial models, the name of a trials column or a numeric vector. Defaults to 1 (Bernoulli).

E

For Poisson models, the name of an offset (expected counts) column or a numeric vector.

svc

Character vector of numeric covariates to give spatially varying slopes. Each must also appear in formula.

svc_model

Latent model for the slope deviations: "besag" (ICAR) or "bym2".

extra_terms

Character vector of additional formula terms, e.g. "f(cluster_idx, model = 'iid')".

priors

Output of svy_priors().

...

Further arguments passed to INLA::inla().

Value

An object of class svy_fit: a list with the INLA fit (inla), the graph, the data used and model settings.

Details

The model for record \(i\) in area \(a\) is $$g(\mu_i) = \beta_0 + x_i^\top \beta + b_a + \sum_k z_{ik} \gamma_{ka}$$ where \(b_a\) is the BYM2 effect and \(\gamma_{ka}\) are the area deviations of the slope for covariate \(z_k\) (from svc). The total area-specific slope is \(\beta_k + \gamma_{ka}\); see svy_svc_effects().

Survey design

INLA fits a model-based analysis and does not use sampling weights. Adjust for the design by including stratification variables (e.g. region and urban/rural) as fixed effects, and consider a cluster-level iid random effect via extra_terms. For design-based small-area prevalence, see the SUMMER and surveyPrev packages.
